You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
criteria and cannot be changed.

Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).

Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.

`check` reports every record whose wire is committed uncompressed: a path `runs/<stamp>/wire.jsonl` that git tracks is a problem naming the record, `runs/<stamp>/wire.jsonl.gz` being the expected form. A `wire.jsonl` that git does not track is a build not yet reviewed and is not a problem. Nothing in `builder.py` changes: it writes `wire.jsonl`, and the attended agent compresses it at the factory's commit. The tests in `test_gate.py` whose docstring names this seed define the behaviour.

After the build, by the attended agent: the wires of the records already committed are compressed, and `AGENTS.md` names the step.

function.description:

function.description:

green, anything else is red. The tests run in a container, with the world read-only and
no network, so this reports on the world as it is on disk. At most 8 checks per run.

function.description: The builder's report: what it changed in the world, and whether the tests pass.

changed.description: The paths you wrote or edited, in order.

did.description: What you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path.

check.description: Green or red: the state of the last check.

unsure.description: What you could not determine or verify.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The gate: a deterministic check of the vault, its changelog and its tags.
3	
4	    uv run gate.py check
5	    uv run gate.py render
6	    uv run gate.py release <version>
7	
8	`check` validates `docs/` and the repository against it, `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md` from
9	the tags, and `release` refuses until everything derived agrees, then tags and renders. Each
10	command prints one line per problem on stdout, starting with the path relative to the root,
11	and exits 1 if there is any; with nothing to report it prints nothing and exits 0. Usage errors
12	go to stderr and exit 2.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import ast
18	import re
19	import subprocess
20	import sys
21	from pathlib import Path
22	
23	USAGE = "usage: gate.py check|render|release <version>"
24	STATUSES = ("open", "spec", "building", "done", "rejected")
25	SEED_FIELDS = {"type", "status", "summary", "value", "effort", "version", "created"}
26	EFFORTS = {"S", "M", "L"}
27	BASE_LANGUAGE = {"this", "file", "formula", "true", "false", "null"}
28	BASE_IDENT = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*")
29	BASE_HEADER = re.compile(r"^(properties|order|sort|groupBy|filters|formulas):\s*(.*)$")
30	BASE_PROPERTY = re.compile(r"property:\s*(.*)$")
31	CREATED = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$")
32	VERSION_NAME = re.compile(r"^v(\d+)\.(\d+)\.md$")
33	VERSION = re.compile(r"^v(\d+)\.(\d+)$")
34	WIKILINK = re.compile(r"\[\[([^\[\]]+)\]\]")
35

37	def _read(path: Path) -> str:
38	    try:
39	        return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
40	    except OSError:
41	        return ""
42

44	def frontmatter(text: str) -> tuple[dict[str, str] | None, str]:
45	    """The `key: value` block between the leading `---` lines, and the body after it."""
46	    lines = text.splitlines()
47	    if not lines or lines[0].strip() != "---":
48	        return None, text
49	    for i in range(1, len(lines)):
50	        if lines[i].strip() == "---":
51	            fields: dict[str, str] = {}
52	            for line in lines[1:i]:
53	                key, sep, value = line.partition(":")
54	                if sep:
55	                    fields[key.strip()] = value.strip()
56	            return fields, "\n".join(lines[i + 1:])
57	    return None, text
58	
59	
60	def _notes(docs: Path) -> list[Path]:
61	    """Every `.md` under `docs/`, the templates excepted."""
62	    templates = docs / "templates"
63	    return [p for p in sorted(docs.rglob("*.md")) if templates not in p.parents]
64	
65	
66	def _git(root: Path, *args: str) -> str:
67	    try:
68	        done = subprocess.run(
69	            ["git", *args], cwd=str(root), capture_output=True, text=True
70	        )
71	    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
72	        return ""
73	    return done.stdout
74	
75	
76	def _tags(root: Path) -> set[str]:
77	    return {line.strip() for line in _git(root, "tag", "-l").splitlines() if line.strip()}
78	
79	
80	def _highest_tag(tags: set[str]) -> str | None:
81	    best, best_key = None, None
82	    for tag in tags:
83	        match = VERSION.match(tag)
84	        if not match:
85	            continue
86	        key = (int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2)))
87	        if best_key is None or key > best_key:
88	            best, best_key = tag, key
89	    return best

92	def _resolve(target: str, docs: Path) -> bool:
93	    """A note in `docs/`, by path or by name, or a `.base` file."""
94	    target = target.strip()
95	    if not target:
96	        return False
97	    direct = docs / target
98	    if direct.is_file():
99	        return True
100	    if direct.suffix == "" and (docs / (target + ".md")).is_file():
101	        return True
102	    name = target.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
103	    stem = name[:-3] if name.endswith(".md") else name
104	    for found in docs.rglob("*"):
105	        if found.is_file() and (found.name == name or found.stem == stem):
106	            return True
107	    return False
108	
109	
110	def _goal_text(body: str) -> bool:
111	    lines = body.splitlines()
112	    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
113	        if line.strip() != "## Goal":
114	            continue
115	        for after in lines[i + 1:]:
116	            if after.strip().startswith("#"):
117	                break
118	            if after.strip():
119	                return True
120	        return False
121	    return False

124	def _test_docstrings(root: Path) -> list[str]:
125	    """The docstrings of every test method or class in a `test*.py` at the root."""
126	    found: list[str] = []
127	    for path in sorted(root.glob("test*.py")):
128	        if not path.is_file():
129	            continue
130	        try:
131	            tree = ast.parse(_read(path))
132	        except SyntaxError:
133	            continue
134	        for node in ast.walk(tree):
135	            if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) or (
136	                isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef))
137	                and node.name.startswith("test")
138	            ):
139	                doc = ast.get_docstring(node)
140	                if doc:
141	                    found.append(doc)
142	    return found

145	def _named_by_a_test(root: Path, stem: str, docstrings: list[str]) -> bool:
146	    pattern = re.compile(rf"seed:\s*{re.escape(stem)}(?![\w-])")
147	    return any(pattern.search(doc) for doc in docstrings)

150	def _unquoted(text: str) -> str:
151	    """An expression with one layer of Obsidian's YAML quotes, around it, removed."""
152	    text = text.strip()
153	    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == text[-1] and text[0] in "\"'":
154	        quote, text = text[0], text[1:-1]
155	        if quote == '"':
156	            text = text.replace('\\"', '"').replace("\\\\", "\\")
157	        else:
158	            text = text.replace("''", "'")
159	    return text
160	
161	
162	def _expression_names(expression: str) -> list[str]:
163	    """The bare identifiers an Obsidian expression names: quoted strings, members (`.name`),
164	    functions (`name(`), `this`, `file`, `formula`, `true`, `false` and `null` removed."""
165	    text = re.sub(r'"[^"]*"', " ", _unquoted(expression))
166	    text = re.sub(r"'[^']*'", " ", text)
167	    names: list[str] = []
168	    for match in BASE_IDENT.finditer(text):
169	        name = match.group()
170	        if match.start() and text[match.start() - 1] == ".":
171	            continue
172	        if text[match.end():].lstrip().startswith("("):
173	            continue
174	        if name in BASE_LANGUAGE:
175	            continue
176	        names.append(name)
177	    return names
178	
179	
180	def _base_named(text: str) -> list[str]:
181	    """Every property `text` names: keys under `properties:`, entries of `order:`, the
182	    `property:` of a `sort` or `groupBy`, and filter and formula expressions."""
183	    named: list[str] = []
184	    lines = text.splitlines()
185	    i = 0
186	    while i < len(lines):
187	        raw = lines[i]
188	        stripped = raw.strip()
189	        indent = len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip())
190	        i += 1
191	        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
192	            continue
193	        header = BASE_HEADER.match(stripped)
194	        if not header:
195	            continue
196	        key, rest = header.group(1), header.group(2).strip()
197	        if key == "order" and rest.startswith("["):
198	            named.extend(rest.strip("[]").split(","))
199	            continue
200	        block: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
201	        while i < len(lines):
202	            line = lines[i]
203	            content = line.strip()
204	            if content and not content.startswith("#"):
205	                if len(line) - len(line.lstrip()) <= indent:
206	                    break
207	                block.append((len(line) - len(line.lstrip()), content))
208	            i += 1
209	        if key == "properties":
210	            child = min((depth for depth, _ in block), default=indent)
211	            for depth, content in block:
212	                if depth == child and ":" in content and not content.startswith("-"):
213	                    named.append(content.split(":", 1)[0].strip())
214	        elif key == "order":
215	            for _, content in block:
216	                if content.startswith("- "):
217	                    named.append(content[2:].strip())
218	        elif key in ("sort", "groupBy"):
219	            for _, content in block:
220	                match = BASE_PROPERTY.search(content)
221	                if match:
222	                    named.append(match.group(1).strip())
223	        else:
224	            if rest:
225	                named.append(rest)
226	            for _, content in block:
227	                if content.startswith("- "):
228	                    named.append(content[2:].strip())
229	                elif ":" in content:
230	                    value = content.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
231	                    if value:
232	                        named.append(value)
233	    return named

237	    """The properties `docs/backlog.base` names that are not seed template fields."""
238	    base = docs / "backlog.base"

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the checkout, until the checkout's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first checkout: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the tools, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the checkout and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the tools refuse the model the same.
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
criteria and cannot be changed.

Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).

Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.

`check` reports every record whose wire is committed uncompressed: a path `runs/<stamp>/wire.jsonl` that git tracks is a problem naming the record, `runs/<stamp>/wire.jsonl.gz` being the expected form. A `wire.jsonl` that git does not track is a build not yet reviewed and is not a problem. Nothing in `builder.py` changes: it writes `wire.jsonl`, and the attended agent compresses it at the factory's commit. The tests in `test_gate.py` whose docstring names this seed define the behaviour.

After the build, by the attended agent: the wires of the records already committed are compressed, and `AGENTS.md` names the step.

3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the checkout, until the checkout's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first checkout: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the tools, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:

13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the checkout, until the checkout's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first checkout: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the tools, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the checkout and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the tools refuse the model the same.
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. Problems go to stdout, one per line, starting with the path; exit 1 when there is any, 2 for a usage error, silence and 0 otherwise. `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md`. `release` also needs a clean tree, `AGENTS.md` changed since the previous tag, a green suite and at least one changelog bullet in the version note.
35	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
36	- `uv run builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the checkout's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Refuses a directory that is not a git checkout, and a checkout with uncommitted or untracked changes, exit 2. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the checkout. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error. The cost and the time are in the record.
37	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a checkout for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
38	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
39	
40	## Not derivable from the repository
41	
42	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. `backlog.base` changes whenever the owner adjusts a view, a filter or an order there, and a note's frontmatter is re-serialised when a property is edited there, in Obsidian's own shape; a frontmatter value that is not valid YAML, such as a bare `{{date}}`, does not survive that. A dirty `docs/` is the owner's content: read the diff and commit it as theirs.
43	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4`; it is one change released in v0.4, not the version.
44	- The notes of v0.1 to v0.4, their changelog and the records before v0.5 say world for the checkout and plane for the tools; those were the observer's words.
45	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.3` are leftovers of past worktrees and share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
46	- The model is DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`. pydantic-ai does not know the name, so `builder.py` carries a profile override; genai-prices has no row for it, so the price table in `builder.py` is the cost source. Thinking is on by default and ignores temperature. The key is never printed or committed.
47	- The history before this repository, v1 and the design that was abandoned for it, is in the owner's Obsidian vault at `/srv/obsidian/vaults/obsidian/03 archive/factory-v1/`. Reference, never a plan.

smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).

Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.

`check` reports every record whose wire is committed uncompressed: a path `runs/<stamp>/wire.jsonl` that git tracks is a problem naming the record, `runs/<stamp>/wire.jsonl.gz` being the expected form. 4	    uv run gate.py check

10	command prints one line per problem on stdout, starting with the path relative to the root,
11	and exits 1 if there is any; with nothing to report it prints nothing and exits 0. Usage errors

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the checkout, until the checkout's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first checkout: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the tools, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the checkout and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the tools refuse the model the same.
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. Problems go to stdout, one per line, starting with the path; exit 1 when there is any, 2 for a usage error, silence and 0 otherwise. `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md`. `release` also needs a clean tree, `AGENTS.md` changed since the previous tag, a green suite and at least one changelog bullet in the version note.
35	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
36	- `uv run builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the checkout's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Refuses a directory that is not a git checkout, and a checkout with uncommitted or untracked changes, exit 2. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the checkout. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error. The cost and the time are in the record.
37	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a checkout for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
38	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
39	
40	## Not derivable from the repository
41	
42	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. `backlog.base` changes whenever the owner adjusts a view, a filter or an order there, and a note's frontmatter is re-serialised when a property is edited there, in Obsidian's own shape; a frontmatter value that is not valid YAML, such as a bare `{{date}}`, does not survive that. A dirty `docs/` is the owner's content: read the diff and commit it as theirs.
43	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4`; it is one change released in v0.4, not the version.
44	- The notes of v0.1 to v0.4, their changelog and the records before v0.5 say world for the checkout and plane for the tools; those were the observer's words.
45	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.3` are leftovers of past worktrees and share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
46	- The model is DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`. pydantic-ai does not know the name, so `builder.py` carries a profile override; genai-prices has no row for it, so the price table in `builder.py` is the cost source. Thinking is on by default and ignores temperature. The key is never printed or committed.
47	- The history before this repository, v1 and the design that was abandoned for it, is in the owner's Obsidian vault at `/srv/obsidian/vaults/obsidian/03 archive/factory-v1/`. Reference, never a plan.

List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
relative to the world root; '.' is the root.

path.description: The directory to list, relative to the world root.

function.name: read
function.description:
Read a file of the world as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.

path.description: The file to read, relative to the world root.

function.name: write
function.description:
Write a file of the world: create it, or replace what is there with `content`.
Directories on the way are created. The tests and the toolchain cannot be written.

path.description: The file to write, relative to the world root.

content.description: The whole text of the file, as it should be afterwards.

function.name: edit
function.description:
Edit a file of the world: replace `old` with `new`, once. `old` must appear in the
file exactly once; if it does not, nothing is changed and the count is reported. The
tests and the toolchain cannot be edited.

path.description: The file to edit, relative to the world root.

old.description: The exact text to replace; include lines around it to make it unique.

new.description: The text to put in its place.

function.name: check
function.description:
Run the world's tests and return the exit code and the tail of the output: exit 0 is
green, anything else is red. The tests run in a container, with the world read-only and
no network, so this reports on the world as it is on disk. At most 8 checks per run.

function.name: final_result
function.description: The builder's report: what it changed in the world, and whether the tests pass.

changed.description: The paths you wrote or edited, in order.

did.description: What you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path.

check.description: Green or red: the state of the last check.

unsure.description: What you could not determine or verify.

3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the checkout, until the checkout's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first checkout: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the tools, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the checkout and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the tools refuse the model the same.

34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. 1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the checkout, until the checkout's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first checkout: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the tools, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the checkout and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the tools refuse the model the same.
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. Problems go to stdout, one per line, starting with the path; exit 1 when there is any, 2 for a usage error, silence and 0 otherwise. `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md`. `release` also needs a clean tree, `AGENTS.md` changed since the previous tag, a green suite and at least one changelog bullet in the version note.
35	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
36	- `uv run builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the checkout's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Refuses a directory that is not a git checkout, and a checkout with uncommitted or untracked changes, exit 2. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the checkout. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error. The cost and the time are in the record.
37	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a checkout for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
38	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
39	
40	## Not derivable from the repository
41	
42	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. `backlog.base` changes whenever the owner adjusts a view, a filter or an order there, and a note's frontmatter is re-serialised when a property is edited there, in Obsidian's own shape; a frontmatter value that is not valid YAML, such as a bare `{{date}}`, does not survive that. A dirty `docs/` is the owner's content: read the diff and commit it as theirs.
43	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4`; it is one change released in v0.4, not the version.
44	- The notes of v0.1 to v0.4, their changelog and the records before v0.5 say world for the checkout and plane for the tools; those were the observer's words.
45	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.3` are leftovers of past worktrees and share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
46	- The model is DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`. pydantic-ai does not know the name, so `builder.py` carries a profile override; genai-prices has no row for it, so the price table in `builder.py` is the cost source. Thinking is on by default and ignores temperature. The key is never printed or committed.
47	- The history before this repository, v1 and the design that was abandoned for it, is in the owner's Obsidian vault at `/srv/obsidian/vaults/obsidian/03 archive/factory-v1/`. Reference, never a plan.

messages.content:
You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
criteria and cannot be changed.

Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).

Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.

`check` reports every record whose wire is committed uncompressed: a path `runs/<stamp>/wire.jsonl` that git tracks is a problem naming the record, `runs/<stamp>/wire.jsonl.gz` being the expected form. A `wire.jsonl` that git does not track is a build not yet reviewed and is not a problem. Nothing in `builder.py` changes: it writes `wire.jsonl`, and the attended agent compresses it at the factory's commit. The tests in `test_gate.py` whose docstring names this seed define the behaviour.

After the build, by the attended agent: the wires of the records already committed are compressed, and `AGENTS.md` names the step.

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the checkout, until the checkout's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first checkout: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the tools, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the checkout and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the tools refuse the model the same.
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. Problems go to stdout, one per line, starting with the path; exit 1 when there is any, 2 for a usage error, silence and 0 otherwise. `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md`. `release` also needs a clean tree, `AGENTS.md` changed since the previous tag, a green suite and at least one changelog bullet in the version note.
35	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
36	- `uv run builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the checkout's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Refuses a directory that is not a git checkout, and a checkout with uncommitted or untracked changes, exit 2. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the checkout. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error. The cost and the time are in the record.
37	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a checkout for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
38	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
39	
40	## Not derivable from the repository
41	
42	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. `backlog.base` changes whenever the owner adjusts a view, a filter or an order there, and a note's frontmatter is re-serialised when a property is edited there, in Obsidian's own shape; a frontmatter value that is not valid YAML, such as a bare `{{date}}`, does not survive that. A dirty `docs/` is the owner's content: read the diff and commit it as theirs.
43	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4`; it is one change released in v0.4, not the version.
44	- The notes of v0.1 to v0.4, their changelog and the records before v0.5 say world for the checkout and plane for the tools; those were the observer's words.
45	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.3` are leftovers of past worktrees and share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
46	- The model is DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`. pydantic-ai does not know the name, so `builder.py` carries a profile override; genai-prices has no row for it, so the price table in `builder.py` is the cost source. Thinking is on by default and ignores temperature. The key is never printed or committed.
47	- The history before this repository, v1 and the design that was abandoned for it, is in the owner's Obsidian vault at `/srv/obsidian/vaults/obsidian/03 archive/factory-v1/`. Reference, never a plan.

2	"""The gate: a deterministic check of the vault, its changelog and its tags.

5	    uv run gate.py render

8	`check` validates `docs/` and the repository against it, `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md` from

45	    """The `key: value` block between the leading `---` lines, and the body after it."""
46	    lines = text.splitlines()

48	        return None, text

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the checkout, until the checkout's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first checkout: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the tools, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the checkout and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the tools refuse the model the same.
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. Problems go to stdout, one per line, starting with the path; exit 1 when there is any, 2 for a usage error, silence and 0 otherwise. `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md`. `release` also needs a clean tree, `AGENTS.md` changed since the previous tag, a green suite and at least one changelog bullet in the version note.
35	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
36	- `uv run builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the checkout's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Refuses a directory that is not a git checkout, and a checkout with uncommitted or untracked changes, exit 2. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the checkout. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error. The cost and the time are in the record.
37	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a checkout for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
38	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
39	
40	## Not derivable from the repository
41	
42	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. `backlog.base` changes whenever the owner adjusts a view, a filter or an order there, and a note's frontmatter is re-serialised when a property is edited there, in Obsidian's own shape; a frontmatter value that is not valid YAML, such as a bare `{{date}}`, does not survive that. A dirty `docs/` is the owner's content: read the diff and commit it as theirs.
43	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4`; it is one change released in v0.4, not the version.
44	- The notes of v0.1 to v0.4, their changelog and the records before v0.5 say world for the checkout and plane for the tools; those were the observer's words.
45	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.3` are leftovers of past worktrees and share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
46	- The model is DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`. pydantic-ai does not know the name, so `builder.py` carries a profile override; genai-prices has no row for it, so the price table in `builder.py` is the cost source. Thinking is on by default and ignores temperature. The key is never printed or committed.
47	- The history before this repository, v1 and the design that was abandoned for it, is in the owner's Obsidian vault at `/srv/obsidian/vaults/obsidian/03 archive/factory-v1/`. Reference, never a plan.

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the checkout, until the checkout's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first checkout: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the tools, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the checkout and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the tools refuse the model the same.
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. Problems go to stdout, one per line, starting with the path; exit 1 when there is any, 2 for a usage error, silence and 0 otherwise. `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md`. `release` also needs a clean tree, `AGENTS.md` changed since the previous tag, a green suite and at least one changelog bullet in the version note.
35	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
36	- `uv run builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the checkout's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Refuses a directory that is not a git checkout, and a checkout with uncommitted or untracked changes, exit 2. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the checkout. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error. The cost and the time are in the record.
37	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a checkout for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
38	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
39	
40	## Not derivable from the repository
41	
42	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. `backlog.base` changes whenever the owner adjusts a view, a filter or an order there, and a note's frontmatter is re-serialised when a property is edited there, in Obsidian's own shape; a frontmatter value that is not valid YAML, such as a bare `{{date}}`, does not survive that. A dirty `docs/` is the owner's content: read the diff and commit it as theirs.
43	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4`; it is one change released in v0.4, not the version.
44	- The notes of v0.1 to v0.4, their changelog and the records before v0.5 say world for the checkout and plane for the tools; those were the observer's words.
45	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.3` are leftovers of past worktrees and share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
46	- The model is DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`. pydantic-ai does not know the name, so `builder.py` carries a profile override; genai-prices has no row for it, so the price table in `builder.py` is the cost source. Thinking is on by default and ignores temperature. The key is never printed or committed.
47	- The history before this repository, v1 and the design that was abandoned for it, is in the owner's Obsidian vault at `/srv/obsidian/vaults/obsidian/03 archive/factory-v1/`. Reference, never a plan.

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the checkout, until the checkout's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first checkout: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the tools, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the checkout and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the tools refuse the model the same.
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. Problems go to stdout, one per line, starting with the path; exit 1 when there is any, 2 for a usage error, silence and 0 otherwise. `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md`. `release` also needs a clean tree, `AGENTS.md` changed since the previous tag, a green suite and at least one changelog bullet in the version note.
35	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
36	- `uv run builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the checkout's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Refuses a directory that is not a git checkout, and a checkout with uncommitted or untracked changes, exit 2. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the checkout. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error. The cost and the time are in the record.
37	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a checkout for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
38	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
39	
40	## Not derivable from the repository
41	
42	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. `backlog.base` changes whenever the owner adjusts a view, a filter or an order there, and a note's frontmatter is re-serialised when a property is edited there, in Obsidian's own shape; a frontmatter value that is not valid YAML, such as a bare `{{date}}`, does not survive that. A dirty `docs/` is the owner's content: read the diff and commit it as theirs.
43	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4`; it is one change released in v0.4, not the version.
44	- The notes of v0.1 to v0.4, their changelog and the records before v0.5 say world for the checkout and plane for the tools; those were the observer's words.
45	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.3` are leftovers of past worktrees and share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
46	- The model is DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`. pydantic-ai does not know the name, so `builder.py` carries a profile override; genai-prices has no row for it, so the price table in `builder.py` is the cost source. Thinking is on by default and ignores temperature. The key is never printed or committed.
47	- The history before this repository, v1 and the design that was abandoned for it, is in the owner's Obsidian vault at `/srv/obsidian/vaults/obsidian/03 archive/factory-v1/`. Reference, never a plan.
